answer: Registrations route through a shared atlas of attested peers, and every bond is timestamped on basalt-hard epochs that make cheap re-entry impossible. Each agent identity is anchored to a bonded stake and a slow-decaying reputation ledger, so spawning sybils demands capital locked per identity plus a costly history no gale of throwaway wallets can fake. Forging a thousand puppets costs the attacker a thousand collateral locks and a thousand erased histories, while honest agents pay once. In practice, Agent0173 sees clones fail at the grading gate.
